target_customer: Spreadsheet users wanting tables, queries and filters in a grid
problem: Spreadsheets lack structure like tables, queries, filtering and search.

founders.name: Ben Vogt
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. Replo is YC S21, so that role came after Protobase.

competitors.name: Airtable
competitors.traction_then: Established product with first funding in 2015

technical_complexity.rationale: A new spreadsheet engine with formulas and a query layer is meaningful engineering for one person.

defensibility.rationale: Funded incumbents offered the same table and query features and a solo founder had no differentiator documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google Sheets and Airtable continued to dominate; Google later shut down its Tables rival in 2025, per a Slashdot item.

market_need_then: Spreadsheets are ubiquitous and Airtable's growth showed demand for structured spreadsheets; no Protobase user data was found.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand material or press found; the protobase.com name could not be confirmed.

outcome_analysis: Protobase was a one person YC W20 company building a structured next generation spreadsheet against well funded rivals such as Airtable. It is listed Inactive and the founder later worked at Replo, but no post-mortem or shutdown notice was found, so the cause is not public. Funding appears limited to a 500 thousand dollar YC convertible note per one aggregator.
notes: The company has no website listed. The 500K convertible note dated 2020-01-01 rests on CB Insights alone and is labeled other. Founding year conflict: YC says 2019, CB Insights 2018. The Airtable source is a 2015 funding article, so traction then is not stated beyond that.
